11. Case managers should however use discretion to apply flexibility where appropriate (e.g. if there was a delay in the customer receiving their award letter).

12. Payment queries should be forwarded to the payment enquiry inbox.

13. New application queries should be directed to gov.uk or the customer can be told to contact by phone if they are unable to use online services.

Authorising changes to approved support

14. A change in the customer’s circumstances or a change in the rates charged for AtW support may mean an increase in the authorised amount of AtW support.

15. Flexibility exists to allow small increases in support without the need for approval of a new business case.

16. The decision to apply flexibility must be confirmed by a Case Manager not previously involved in assessing the customer’s needs. Confirmation that flexibility has applied must be recorded.

17. Flexibility cannot be allowed if the total amount of increases, including the increase currently being considered, since the last signed authorisation is £500 or more.

18. Flexibility cannot be allowed if it takes the total amount approved into a higher approval bracket.

Example

If an operations manager has authorised expenditure of £59,900, increases of, or totalling £100 or more cannot be given. This would take the total amount approved to the level where senior operations manager authorisation is needed.

Changes to a customer’s health

19. Some health conditions can switch unpredictably between periods when symptoms are stable to periods of deterioration. When a customer’s health deteriorates, there’s likely to be an impact on their ability to do their job. It may not be possible to fully re-assess the customer’s requirements until their health stabilises.

20. Record details of the change and consider booking a review at a suitable date in the future.

21. Consider whether temporary support could be put in place. This will enable the customer to retain their employment while their needs are reassessed or until they recover from the temporary change in their health or condition. Respond sensitively and flexibly to customers in these circumstances.

22. If increased support is needed, it must be supported by a revised business case and approved before more AtW payments are made.

23. The cost share decision applied to the existing award will apply to the extra needs for elements where cost share applies.

24. A change in the customer’s condition may lead to a reduction in the support required. Record the change and advise the customer that their requirements will be fully re-assessed at the end of the current AtW period.

25. The customer/employer will continue to claim repayment for elements of the AtW funding that are still required. If the customer has a support worker supplied by an agency, advise the agency of the changes in support needed.

26. Where the customer or their employer, employ the support worker, AtW can continue to fund the normal level of support for a maximum of 4 weeks. The profiled expenditure for the customer should be left unchanged, so that if the customer’s condition deteriorates again, the full amount of support originally agreed can be provided without delay.

27. All claims must be checked to make sure overpayments are not made.

Change in personal details

28. Most changes in personal details will have no impact on AtW support. A change of address is likely to have an effect on Travel to Work (TtW) costs or on a support worker’s activities.

29. Customers or OGD can report changes in the customer’s personal details.

30. Update the customer record with all relevant changes and details of any support that’s been reassessed.

31. Check if there is a live payee record for the caller. If so, arrange for payment action to be taken.

32. Notify any other relevant OGD or agency that needs the information. Record actions taken.

Change of name

33. If the customer’s name changes, update the customer’s record. Verify the bank account details and update them if necessary.

Change of address

34. If the customer changes address this is likely to have an effect on TtW costs or on support worker’s activities. You must:

review all support to ensure it’s still appropriate and meeting the customer’s needs

adjust the support where appropriate

update the system with all relevant changes

Changes to employment

Same employer, different job

35. A new job with the same employer may result in a change in support.

36. Ensure the job is new by confirming new duties or change in earnings.

37. If it’s a new job, the case is treated as a new application. You must:

consider if reasonable adjustments are appropriate

create a new job entry and record the AtW start date

reassess the support needed

identify changes

apply cost share if appropriate

create an updated business case for extra costs and submit for approval.

38. If new elements of support are to be supplied, monitor delivery and consider the need for temporary solutions until the required solutions are in place.

New employer (new owner of business), same job

39. Under the TUPE regulations, the new owner of a business is obliged to take on the contractual obligations of their predecessor. This includes the cost sharing agreements with AtW.

40. If a customer makes contact because a new employer has taken over the business you must:

update the employment details

contact the new employer to confirm they will carry forward the existing support arrangements

make sure the new employer is aware of their ownership and maintenance obligations for any equipment provided

41. If the employer wishes to renegotiate support arrangements, for example providing a support worker from internal staff rather than on going cost share, you must review the business case.

42. The change can be approved if it means a reduction or no change in the AtW support.

contact the customer by their usual method of contact to explain that the application is unable to proceed

update DiSC notes with the reasons for the customer’s application being closed

issue rejection letter AWT05NARL to notify the customer in writing, with free text

“From 1 April 2022, Access to Work support is changing for civil servants. All government departments will be responsible for arranging workplace assessments and adjustment support. Please speak to your employer, manager or where applicable, your Workplace Adjustment Team to arrange support. Access to Work support will be limited to the Mental Health Support Service only.”

New Application or Renewal received from a government department employee on or before 31 March 2022

17. When a new application or renewal is received from a government department employee, you must identify and record their type of employment in DiSC as a civil servant or a public servant. If the customer is unsure of their status, they must ask their manager.

Actions for Case Managers

18.

Step Action

1. When you create the customer record, you must enter the type of government department employment in the Employment Sector field in DiSC’s Job page (if not already updated). Identify and record:

Civil Servant as ‘Government Departments’, or

Public Servant as ‘Other Public Sector’

2. Issue the award letter ATW01. If the customer is a civil servant, select the appropriate dropdown

3. In all cases a note must be created in the additional details box of the customer screen with the title ‘OGD Customer’ including:

the letters and claim forms issued with the appropriate text added to the award letter

if the customer is a civil servant, the following text with the customer’s award end date:

‘Fixed award end date of xx/xx/xx – Civil Servant. Do not extend funding beyond this date’

Ministerial department (up to and including 31 March 2022)

Note: Up to and including 31 March 2022, AtW funding depends on the department the person works for rather than their status as a civil servant or a public servant.

19. Ministerial departments of the Westminster government fund all adjustments for staff directly employed by them and based at any location.

20. Access to Work support is not available to employees of Ministerial departments unless covered in exceptions and variations.

Exceptions and variations (up to and including 31 March 2022)

Non ministerial departments (up to and including 31 March 2022)

21. Non ministerial departments do not fund adjustments for their staff, therefore, AtW is appropriate.

See: Departments, agencies and public bodies for a full list of non ministerial departments.

Agencies and other public bodies (up to and including 31 March 2022)

22. Ministerial departments do not fund adjustments for staff employed by their agencies and other public bodies. AtW will fund adjustments required by their staff.

23. The Home Office (this includes Border Force, UK Visas and Immigration and HM Passport Office) and the Department for Work and Pensions are exceptions as they do fund adjustments for staff employed by their agencies and other public bodies.

See: Departments, agencies and public bodies for a full list of non ministerial departments.

Mental Health Support Service (up to and including 31 March 2022)

24. Mental Health Support Service (MHSS) referrals are available to employees of any ministerial department.

25. The cost of any recommendations made by MHSS for employees of ministerial departments cannot be met by AtW.

Ministry of Defence (up to and including 31 March 2022)

26. The Ministry of Defence only fund adjustments for staff employed at their main building in Whitehall.

Child Maintenance Group (up to and including 31 March 2022)

27. The Child Maintenance Group fund adjustments for their staff. AtW funding is not appropriate.

Assessments (up to and including 31 March 2022)

28. AtW can provide assessments for people employed in any ministerial department other than DWP.

New application for support received from a government department employee on or after 1 April 2022

29. From 1 April 2022, civil servants can no longer make new applications for Access to Work (AtW) support.

Note: Any application for support made up to and including 31 March 2022 where support was awarded, the customer continues to receive AtW support until the end of that award period.

30. If the customer is employed as a civil servant, a new application cannot proceed. You must signpost the customer to:

their employer to arrange support.

Mental Health Support Services if appropriate

31. If the customer is employed as a public servant, their new AtW application can proceed.

32. Where the customer’s status is disputed or their status as a civil servant or public servant cannot be confirmed, the CM must ask their Line Manager for support.

Change of Circumstances received from civil servant customers on or after 1 April 2022

33. Awards in place before 31 March 2022 are honoured in their entirety, up to a maximum of 3 years.

34. This means that customers with an award running beyond 1 April 2022 can continue to receive support from AtW up to their existing award end date, including any reported changes in circumstances during the period of their award that relate to the existing element(s) they have been awarded. AtW will maintain and update the award, but the award end date must not be extended.

Example

A civil servant customer has a Travel to Work (TtW) existing award which runs beyond 1 April 2022 and the customer’s TtW costs increase after 1 April 2022. This element is part of their original award, and this is a change of circumstances. The customer can receive an increased award, but the length of award cannot be extended.

passages.quote:
to recruit a new employee as a support worker

64. AtW can repay:

a full salary

national insurance contributions

pension, leave and sickness payments

recruitment costs including advertising

costs of a temporary SW to cover the sick employed SW

65. Rates of pay should be looked at again at the yearly review or if the level of support changes.

66. If the SW is off sick for a period of time and the customer is remaining in work, it’s possible to fund this via AtW and should be considered to ensure the retention of the customer’s job. It’s usual to agree to pay for the SW if they or the customer are sick for up to 4 weeks in a rolling 12-month period from the first period of sickness.

67. AtW can pay recruitment costs up to 5% of the SW’s gross salary. This covers the cost of adding the new employee to the payroll and any other HR activities. This must only be done if the employer asks for it. AtW will repay the full cost when an employer provides evidence to show that they have had to pay an amount greater than this percentage. They must provide a breakdown to demonstrate how this amount is made up.

68. Redundancy and notice payments costs can be paid. Don’t profile redundancy or notice payments into the applicant’s profile. These costs must be profiled when they occur.

69. Costs cannot be applied for retrospectively and would be unlikely to be paid if such an application was received.

70. Case Managers need to agree a fixed period for which AtW will pay to cover unexpected absences such as sick leave. This must be included in the offer letter outlining the agreed support including the number of hours and rate of pay etc.

71. If a customer accepts the responsibilities of being their SW’s employer they might need additional support to fulfil this role properly. These costs can be approved through AtW where the need is related to their disability, illness or health condition.

72. Case Managers must agree an extra number of hours initially, but keep this under review. Don’t meet this need through an increase in the hourly rate paid to the SW.

73. Customers and SWs who wish to find out their employment position must be told to contact their local HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) office.

74. HMRC has a Helpline for new employers.

Telephone: 0300 200 3211

Text phone: 0300 200 3212

75. If any financial liability is incurred as a result of a customer being considered an employer by the HMRC, Case Managers may arrange for the customer to be reimbursed from this element. In all such cases, tell the AtW policy team of the details at once.

76. Customers who use family or friends to provide SW help are equally subject to the considerations above.

Support workers booked through an agency

77. If the customer or employer wishes to use an alternative supplier, Case Managers must confirm that the rate quoted is reasonable.

78. All quotes should be a total amount, including all support, travels costs and any necessary booking fees. This allows the AtW Case Manager to see which agency offers the most cost effective solution for the entire service.

Payment for a support worker

79. Payment for a SW will only be made for the days on which a customer would usually work or for other days for example, leave written in the SW’s contract of employment.

80. These costs must be confirmed with the employer of the SW. Case Managers can now obtain details from the SW Contract verbally if the employer agrees. Case Managers will record details from the contract of employment in the Additional Info (Payment Team) field under the appropriate Element.

81. Customers or employers who do not wish to share this information by telephone can continue to post or email (if a reasonable adjustment) any Contract of employment / Time Sheet / Wage slip to Access to Work for Support Workers costs. Case managers will transfer the required contractual information into the Additional Info (Payment Team) field under the appropriate Element.

82. The following information must be checked with the SW Claim form to validate and issue payment:

Full Name of Support Worker

Number of hours worked per week

Total salary paid

Total NI & Pension contributions made

Any annual leave and/or sick leave taken during the period being claimed for

83. Payment officers must check in the Additional Info (Payment Team) field under the appropriate Element before approving/rejecting any claims.

84. Personal information should be redacted from the Timesheet / Wage slip. Only the information required to validate the claim will be used.

85. Where the SW is employed by the customer or customer’s Employer they will continue to be paid if the customer is sick for up to 4 weeks, in a 12-month period from the first period of sickness

86. Case Managers must profile all costs, inclusive of VAT, over a 52-week period as the SW may be entitled to holiday/sickness payments from the customer/employer under the Working Time Regulations introduced in October 1998.

87. Under the regulations, a worker is entitled to 5.6 weeks’ leave or at least 28 days if a person were to work a 5-day week. This isn’t in addition to contractual rights.

See: holiday entitlement on the GOV.UK website.

88. AtW will pay for these weeks leave, as it’s an extra cost that would not have been relevant had the employer or customer not needed to employ the SW.

See: Health & Safety Executive website for specific information.

See: Pay and work rights on the GOV.UK website.

See: The Working Time Regulations on the Heath and Safety Executive website.

Flexible personalisation

89. Build in a tolerance to allow for small increases in support without the need for approval of a new business case and based on need only.

90. The percentage tolerance range must be up to 5%, and must only be applied after all reasons have been included in the reaching of the yearly profile.
